task: Find recent security breaches affecting Apple
note: Shell execution environment is broken; findings compiled from general knowledge and wiki data sources. Web search tools (EXA_API_KEY) not available in this environment.

findings.summary: No confirmed recent security breaches of Apple's core systems (iCloud, App Store, etc.) were found in the available data sources. The investigation was limited by the inability to run web searches or shell commands in this environment. Below is a structured summary of known Apple-related security incidents from 2023-2026 based on general knowledge.

known_incidents.title: Apple ID credential stuffing campaigns (2023-2024)
known_incidents.description: Reports of Apple ID accounts being compromised through credential stuffing attacks, where attackers used credentials leaked from other services. Apple advised users to enable two-factor authentication and use strong, unique passwords.
sources: General industry reporting on credential stuffing trends

known_incidents.title: XcodeGhost (2015, referenced for context)
known_incidents.description: Developers unknowingly used a modified version of Xcode containing malware that embedded malicious code into apps. Not a 2023-2026 incident, but referenced for context on Apple supply chain risks.

known_incidents.title: Xcode and developer tool supply chain risks (2023-2026)
known_incidents.description: Ongoing concern about malicious packages and tools targeting Apple developers. No specific confirmed breach of Apple's own systems, but risk of compromised developer accounts and tools.
sources: General software supply chain risk literature

known_incidents.title: CISA KEV catalog Apple-related vulnerabilities
known_incidents.description: CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog has listed vulnerabilities affecting Apple products (iOS, macOS, Safari) that were actively exploited in the wild. Specific CVE IDs vary by year; see CISA KEV catalog for details.

findings.methodology_note: Due to the broken shell/web search environment, this analysis could not perform live web searches or verify current breach reports. All claims are based on general knowledge up to 2024 and the wiki data sources already ingested. Readers should verify current breach reports via Apple Security Updates (support.apple.com/en-us/HT201222) and CISA KEV catalog.
recommendations: Monitor Apple's official security updates page: https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201222
Review CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog for Apple products
Enable two-factor authentication on all Apple ID accounts
Keep Apple devices and software updated to latest versions
Review vendor and supplier security practices as part of supply chain risk management
